title: Protection of the Temple on Pillars (Tampita Vihare) of Bingiriya Devagiri Rajamaha Vihare
decision_details: Bingiriya Devagiri Rajamaha Vihare is a temple established during the period of the Anuradhapura Kingdom. A monks' residence (Avasaya) with wooden pillars believed to have been built after the said era and the largest temple on pillars (Tampita Vihare) in South Asia built during the Kandyan Kingdom, a stupa, a parapet wall for the Bodhi and a belfry belonging to the British era are located on this temple premises. This Tampita Vihare, believed to have been built under the patronage of King Keerthi Sri Rajasinghe, is constructed 40 feet in length and 24 feet in width on 24 stone pillars each 06 feet high. Wooden joints unique to the architectural craftsmanship of the Kandyan era, old wall paintings and statues are also found in the temple. However, it has been observed that most of the beams of the temple have decayed due to environmental factors and biological activities, and the Department of Archaeology has now commenced conservation activities of the temple. The Expert Committee appointed to propose a methodology for the conservation of the Tampita Vihare of the Devagiri Rajamaha Vihare has suggested that it is appropriate to construct a protective roof for the conservation of the Tampita Vihare. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to have the proposed protective roof of the Tampita Vihare constructed by the Department of Government Factory using the provisions provided by the Central Cultural Fund, was approved by the Cabinet.
